finding_verdicts.title: Share semantic ledger validation without the synthetic YAML/read-model round trip

evidence.observation: After the real YAML parse, decisions validation creates and serializes another Document, then calls parseLedger. Changed writes validate the working mapping and the final formatted mapping as well.
parseLedger performs ingress parsing, semantic validation, sorting/current selection and hashing; the state validator discards its read model.
Malformed YAML, aliases/tags, duplicate pairs, supersedes, source limit and large-journal assertions provide regression targets, not executed performance evidence.

finding_verdicts.existing_mechanism_check: The AJV map already caches compiled validators. It does not remove the synthetic ledger parse. Original Documents retain comments and synchronization behavior; their removal is not recommended.
finding_verdicts.concrete_scenario: Loading a valid decisions artifact invokes this extra conversion even when only validity is requested. A normal changed mutation takes this path at multiple validation points.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Use one internal ledger data validator from both parseLedger and state.validate. Keep byte-ingress YAML/UTF-8 safety, final formatted-output parse and validation, exact limits/error categories, and read-model construction for actual ledger readers. Preserve synthetic serialization-size acceptance or explicitly separate any change to that contract.
finding_verdicts.guarantees_to_preserve: Do not replace semantic checks with AJV alone; retain JSON-only values, duplicate/supersedes validation, exact revisions, comments, final dependency rereads, response preflight, 64-receipt retention and temp-sync-rename commit.
finding_verdicts.validation_plan: Compare acceptance and error parity across malformed/legacy/large/format-expanded inputs; instrument parse/serialization/read-model counts separately from freshness reads. Retain stale-writer and restart-replay tests. No test or experiment was run.
finding_verdicts.expected_effect: Less transient YAML/read-model allocation; actual user-visible effect unknown.
finding_verdicts.complexity: Medium internal refactor and semantic/limit parity tests; no public API or dependency change.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for redundant work, conditional on parity for implementation feasibility.

finding_verdicts.title: Treat an authenticated replay-generation hint as a benchmark-first storage-contract candidate
finding_verdicts.classification: source-confirmed history scan; value of persisted-hint change remains an unmeasured hypothesis

evidence.observation: The evidence-only replay reader enumerates generation names and hashes hypothetical heads. The normal replay path already receives plan.nextRevision and loads it directly.
Session eligibility separately rejects unresolved locks, rereads original operation bytes and compares every actual target's after-digest.

Operation is schema version 1 with additionalProperties:false and no next_revision field. An added optional field is not readable by existing strict readers merely because new readers support legacy records.
Exact lost-response result/context, ordered request binding, corruption/lock/source-drift rejection, competing actors and one-attempt limits are asserted.

finding_verdicts.existing_mechanism_check: Existing replay already avoids repeating durable effects. No generic idempotency repair or optimization to ordinary known-plan replay is justified. There is no direct persisted selected-generation field in the inspected operation record.
finding_verdicts.narrowing_reason: Keep only a conditional benchmark/design candidate. 'Backward-compatible' must mean a documented reader/version rollout, not simply adding an optional field to today's closed version-1 record. No current workload establishes that this low-frequency scan warrants a storage-contract change.
finding_verdicts.concrete_scenario: For evidence-only replay of one unchanged completed operation, increasing unrelated valid generation filenames increases enumeration and possible head-candidate hashing. Match position is filesystem-order dependent and no elapsed-time claim follows.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: First measure the existing evidence-only lookup over retained-history scales. Only if material, design a versioned authenticated revision selector in the existing operation record with explicit old-reader policy and a legacy fallback. Verify the recorded head after-digest, full generation and request digest; never select latest or trust the hint alone.
finding_verdicts.guarantees_to_preserve: Retained exact result/intent identity, current effect/lock checks, inspected recovery ownership, fail-closed corruption, digest/path checks and atomically updated operation evidence. Do not create a secondary mutable index or global history cache.
finding_verdicts.validation_plan: Benchmark directory materialization and candidate hashes separately from generation verification; add old/new-reader and legacy/hint mismatch fixtures before any contract change. Retain restart, lost-response, changed-target and concurrent-recovery assertions.
finding_verdicts.expected_effect: Potentially remove history-dependent selection work only from evidence-only replay; full verification remains.
finding_verdicts.complexity: Medium contract evolution, not a small transparent field addition.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for scan and closed-schema evidence; practical gain unknown.
finding_verdicts.deferred_design_question: Before implementation, what is the supported policy for older processes reading a store after a newer process writes revision hints? This is not required to accept the narrowed benchmark-first audit recommendation.

finding_verdicts.title: Consume the existing document snapshot in current Definition/Technical preflight

evidence.observation: Current preflight discards listProductDocuments(limit:1), then reloads candidate, registry and every draft document and parses the documents.
The same discarded-list path precedes the Technical loader's own complete loop.

Listing loads the complete candidate snapshot, parsed documents and draft membership inventory before slicing metadata. Its loader does not replace the callers' document-digest and specialized registry checks.
An existing request-scoped consumer reuses snapshot candidate/document/parse values while retaining specialized validation and direct-edit digest checks.
Replay member-order independence, sensitive-input no-write rejection and CRLF preservation are asserted.
Missing upstream PRD, foreign references and stale context reject without effects.
The Roadmap snapshot pattern has a regression ensuring that weaker generic snapshot validation cannot substitute for stricter registry field validation.

finding_verdicts.existing_mechanism_check: Immutable full-generation and Markdown parse reuse already exists inside an audit, but Definition/Technical do not expose an owning outer withProductObjectReads scope in these loaders. The nested list scope ends before their second mutable document-read loop. Do not equate all repeated reads with missing storage caching.
finding_verdicts.concrete_scenario: A current successful semantic authoring preflight with several registered documents processes the full set for the list call and again in its own loader; limit:1 does not bound snapshot work.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Replace the discarded list call with loadProductDocumentSnapshot and reuse its values within that same requireCurrent=true preflight. Keep specialized validateRegistry, identity/artifact checks, digest/direct-edit checks, provenance/upstream rules and membership validation. Do not force current-snapshot loading into requireCurrent=false replay/recovery paths.
finding_verdicts.guarantees_to_preserve: No cross-request mutable draft cache; do not share preflight evidence through lock acquisition or recovery. Keep transaction target freshness, exact replay, source/path/link/size checks, domain validation and unchanged-byte write avoidance.
finding_verdicts.validation_plan: Instrument read/parse counts and output/operation equality; add multi-document, direct edit, malformed registry, inventory and stale-target no-write cases. Retain the selected replay, sensitive-input, CRLF and upstream tests.
finding_verdicts.expected_effect: Reduce duplicate same-preflight document acquisition/parsing; no claimed model-time saving.
finding_verdicts.complexity: Small-to-medium two-loader internal change with specialized-validation regressions.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for the discarded snapshot; runtime magnitude unknown.

finding_verdicts.title: Reuse requirement parsing without silently weakening repeated-read conflict detection
finding_verdicts.classification: source-confirmed repeated parsing; read-elimination equivalence not established

evidence.observation: Each prepared batch member calls verifyRequirements; it parses the specification and can also perform the legacy source reread or decisions load. Every member is validated before append.
requirementSource reads/decodes and builds a Markdown tree on every invocation. There is no request-local RequirementSource cache here.
Each screen and action repeats requirement validation after design/catalog/structural checks.
readDependency compares each observed version against the first registered version, in addition to final dependency verification. A repeated observed change rejects immediately.
Additive/no-op behavior, invalid-member atomic rejection and stale-write diagnostics are asserted.

Tests deliberately retain both callback-time repeated-load conflict detection and final-read verification. They do not establish that initial-plus-final observations are equivalent to all intermediate observation points.
Planning has an explicitly local source snapshot, but that existing different caller lifecycle does not prove equivalence for every repeated-read scenario.

finding_verdicts.existing_mechanism_check: A 1-20-member additive atomic batch and durable no-op/receipt behavior already exist. Read guards track versions rather than parsed sources. The finding is not a request for another batch API.
finding_verdicts.narrowing_reason: The proposal combines eliminating parse work with eliminating repeated source observations. With the current guards, an A-to-B-to-A source edit can be rejected if an intermediate existing read observes B even though final bytes are A. Initial-plus-final checking alone does not preserve that particular rejection. This is an observation-window difference, not a claim of serializable isolation or protection against arbitrary external edits.
finding_verdicts.concrete_scenario: A 20-member guarded batch reparses one unchanged specification repeatedly. For the preservation counterexample, edit the dependency to B before a middle read and restore A before final verification: today's middle read rejects; removing it changes that outcome. This counterexample was derived from source, not executed.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: First reuse the parsed requirement representation by exact bytes/hash and strictness inside the mutation-owned invocation while retaining existing readDependency observation points, fallback semantics and validation order. Eliminating repeated filesystem/hash observations is a separate snapshot-consistency decision, not automatically included in parse reuse. Never add a process-global mutable source cache.
finding_verdicts.guarantees_to_preserve: Every identifier/member remains checked in order; preserve strict/legacy behavior and first-failing-member diagnostics, full experience validation, final guards, no-op revisions, one atomic append, response preflight and exact receipts/retry semantics.
finding_verdicts.validation_plan: Instrument parsing independently of reads at batch sizes 1/2/20. Add strict/legacy, first/middle/last invalid-member, changed-before-final and observed transient-edit cases. Require no write and unchanged diagnostics for rejected batches. No runtime validation occurred.
finding_verdicts.expected_effect: Fewer Markdown AST constructions without claiming fewer filesystem reads or changed consistency semantics.
finding_verdicts.complexity: Small-to-medium internal parsed-source ownership; broader snapshot semantics would need a separate contract review.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for parse repetition and read-guard distinction; relative runtime cost unmeasured.

duplication_links.relationship: Same general local-reuse theme, but not the same source or transaction/read-guard contract.

Missing token references, registration/binding, invalid export and local-versus-external result statuses are asserted.
Token output scope is explicit; invalid output selection rejects atomically. These authority gates are unrelated to parser reuse.

12,500-emoji exact reconstruction, bounded previews/portions and foreign/stale/query-bound cursor rejection are asserted.

finding_verdicts.title: Pack product review batches against the exact success envelope
finding_verdicts.classification: source-confirmed budget mismatch; public failing fixture and savings unmeasured

evidence.observation: Review text can contain arbitrary exact source text. Local fits checks only 24 KiB structured bytes; first-item shrinking and fitted-prefix behavior already exist. Complete-only receipts are computed separately.
The shared helper constructs text and structured copies and enforces both 24 KiB and escaped 64 KiB budgets.
The final guard runs after scenario execution and converts an over-budget whole success into RESULT_LIMIT.
Exact source batches already budget both envelope copies while sharing one LoadedState.
A regression fixture explicitly distinguishes structured-fit from escaped-wire rejection.

The inspected Unicode direct-batch test checks structured size, continuation and receipts; separate tests preserve atomic record batches/replay/final consistency. These do not reproduce the escaping-heavy public get-batch case.

finding_verdicts.existing_mechanism_check: Final rejection already prevents oversized wire success. This is avoidable read/retry work, not an uncapped-response vulnerability. Batch API, pending filtering, adaptive first portion and local object-read scope already exist.
finding_verdicts.concrete_scenario: Several escaping-heavy exact blocks can be accepted under the structured cap yet fail the final duplicated/escaped envelope cap, discarding the useful fitted prefix. Exact public threshold remains unexecuted.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Use boundedSuccessResult as the Boolean predicate on the real context-bearing candidate envelope. Retain first-item shrinking, fitted-prefix stop, item order, partial continuations and explicit error when no portion fits. Do not raise caps or truncate evidence.
finding_verdicts.guarantees_to_preserve: Frozen source verification, complete-only receipts, stable cursor/receipt identity independent of page size, read-only request isolation and final whole-result guard. Mutation batch atomicity is a separate guarantee and is not changed.
finding_verdicts.validation_plan: Create a deterministic public stdio case fitting structured but exceeding escaped-wire bytes, then reconstruct all text and compare final receipts. Cover ordinary Unicode, pending-only and minimal-single-item failures as controls. No test was run.
finding_verdicts.expected_effect: Return useful bounded prefixes instead of avoidable full-batch RESULT_LIMIT retries for affected inputs.
finding_verdicts.complexity: Small predicate replacement; moderate discriminating-fixture work.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for mismatched predicates; specific public reproduction unmeasured.

finding_verdicts.title: Bind cold lazy schema compilation to one startup-verified immutable contract snapshot
finding_verdicts.classification: source-confirmed lifecycle mismatch under in-place replacement; operational impact hypothesis

evidence.observation: Artifact digests/stamp are verified and the returned identity is captured once. The original schema bytes are not supplied to lazy loaders.
A state-kind validator's first use reads its packaged schema asynchronously from disk and then caches the compiled function.
One promise deduplicates product record-schema compilation, but the first read remains lazy and disk-based.
Tool contracts/input validation are eager; output validation invokes the independently lazy product schema owner after scenario work.
runtime_info exposes the captured identity; the inspected registry does not make identity availability a universal authorization gate.

Existing tests require running A to keep A's identity after same-version file replacement, and check unavailable startup identity/new-process changed-contract identity. They do not exercise A's first cold lazy schema validation after replacement.

finding_verdicts.existing_mechanism_check: Startup digests, eager input validators, cached state validators and promise-shared product compilation already solve repeated routine construction and honest identity reporting. They do not bind a cold post-startup schema read to A's startup bytes. Warm validators and immutable-version installation paths do not exhibit the proposed replacement window.
finding_verdicts.narrowing_reason: Accept the contract-coherence fix only under the explicit cold-validator/in-place-replacement scenario. Do not promote it as measured startup optimization or use it to introduce an unrelated universal runtime-identity authorization gate. The source establishes a possible mixed contract, not a current installed-runtime incident.
finding_verdicts.concrete_scenario: A starts and captures A identity/contracts but has not used a lazy record/state validator. Its packaged schema path is replaced with B before first validation. That validation reads B while A still advertises A. The existing A/B test changes executable bytes and checks identity, not cold validation behavior.
finding_verdicts.replacement_minimal_recommendation: Capture the fixed packaged-schema bytes within the serving initialization lifecycle and verify those bytes against the same artifact digest evidence used by startup identity. Lazy compilation may remain, but must consume that snapshot. Reuse existing immutable schema ownership where practical; keep domain-specific validation separate. Fail the affected contract initialization before side-effecting scenario work if its snapshot cannot be coherently established; any blanket policy for identity-unavailable processes is separate scope.
finding_verdicts.guarantees_to_preserve: A remains A until restart; retain schema self-validation, supported definitions, Unicode/domain/sensitivity checks, safe diagnostics and explicit refresh guidance. Never share mutable request state or Ajv error arrays across awaits; do not hash all artifacts per request or cache live workflow data globally.
finding_verdicts.validation_plan: Extend isolated copied-package A/B tests with cold product output and one cold state-kind validator; assert A semantics/identity, coherent restarted B and safe inconsistent startup handling. Include warm-validator and immutable-path controls, concurrent error isolation and no-real-home/store mutation. No replacement experiment or timing was executed.
finding_verdicts.expected_effect: Avoid potential mixed-contract diagnostics/retry failures; initialization speed/memory benefit is unmeasured and secondary.
finding_verdicts.complexity: Medium startup/schema ownership change with bounded immutable process-lifetime data; further eager-validator consolidation is optional and outside the minimal change.
finding_verdicts.confidence: High for the lifetime mismatch; operational frequency and real deployment applicability unknown.
